methods.label: Method 1: Track the stem and arms
methods.explanation:
Track the stem along the positive \(y\)-axis and the two arms of the F. Since rotations and reflections preserve the shape and lengths, these features let us recognize the final image.

After the \(90^\circ\) clockwise rotation, the stem lies along the positive \(x\)-axis. Both arms extend downward, with the longer arm at the right end.

Reflecting in the \(y\)-axis reverses left and right. The stem now lies along the negative \(x\)-axis, both arms still extend downward, and the longer arm is at the left end.

The half turn moves the stem back to the positive \(x\)-axis and turns the arms upward. The longer arm is now at the right end. This is the final image shown in choice \(\boxed{E}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses elementary geometric tracking of quarter turns, a reflection, and a half turn, appropriate for AMC 10.

methods.label: Method 2: Compose coordinate rules
methods.explanation:
Tracking an arbitrary point gives one rule for the entire figure. Let \((x,y)\) be any point of the original F. A clockwise quarter turn changes a horizontal displacement into a downward displacement and a vertical displacement into a rightward displacement, so its image is \((y,-x)\).

Reflection in the \(y\)-axis changes the sign of the horizontal coordinate. A half turn around the origin then changes the signs of both coordinates. Applying these operations in the stated order gives
\[
(x,y)\longmapsto(y,-x)\longmapsto(-y,-x)\longmapsto(y,x).
\]
Thus the final transformation exchanges the coordinates. The original stem on the positive \(y\)-axis moves to the positive \(x\)-axis, and the rightward arms become upward arms, with the longer arm on the right. The final image is choice \(\boxed{E}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses elementary coordinate pairs and sign changes for rotations and reflections, within AMC 10 geometry.
